what_this_is: Step 3's comparison. The 1923 professional takeoff's quantities are scored against quantities computed from geometry taken off the FIGURED GROUND PLAN (Plate 8), independently of the dimension columns the takeoff was squared from. No threshold was revised, nothing frozen was edited and the self-validation guard was not weakened.
correctness_note: A unit test on synthetic geometry establishes CORRECTNESS -- that the formula computes the quantity it documents, with the deductions and conventions it documents. It establishes NOTHING about accuracy against a real building, and is never reported as accuracy.

self_validation_guard_before_and_after.what_this_shows: R2 refused #265's three ceiling comparisons at a residual of EXACTLY 0.0 because the geometry and the reference were the same numbers. arms.arm: #265: geometry from the takeoff's own dimension columns

heights_are_figured_on_no_plate.finding: ACROSS ALL TEN PLATES, INCLUDING BOTH SECTIONS, NO STOREY HEIGHT AND NO ROOM HEIGHT IS FIGURED. The two sections (Plates 5 and 6) carry a scale bar and not one dimension. The 8'0" the plasterer squares his walls at exists ONLY in his dimension columns. It is therefore NOT recoverable from the drawings by any method the schema admits -- MeasurementMethod has no member for a value scaled off a raster -- so F2 wall paintable area ABSTAINS for every room of this project. This is #263's height finding reproduced on a complete professional drawing set a century old.
heights_are_figured_on_no_plate.consequence: F2 wall paintable area abstains for every room of this project on WALL_HEIGHT_NOT_STATED, and would abstain on OPENING_SCHEDULE_NOT_COMPLETE as well

convention_audit.source: Banister Fletcher & H. P. Fletcher, Quantities, 9th edition

rules.our_frozen_choice: CEILING_IS_FLAT_AND_COINCIDENT_WITH_FLOOR = True; no cornice or chimney-breast deduction
rules.fletcher_rule: Measure the ceilings the full dimensions between the walls; but where cornices occur, it is customary to make a deduction of the width of the cornice upon each dimension for width and length of ceiling. ... Make the deductions for chimney breasts, &c.
rules.cited: p.128, leaf 147 (prose chapter, Plasterer — Internal Work)
rules.worked_example_in_source: a room 20'0" x 16'0" with a 12" cornice is booked 19'0" x 15'0" = 285 sq ft instead of 320 sq ft

rules.formula: F2 wall paintable area — the skirting band
rules.fletcher_rule: Rendering to walls is measured the length by the height, the latter being taken from the top of the skirting grounds to the ceiling, and where there is a cornice it is customary to deduct from this dimension half the height of the cornice.
rules.note: This is a DIRECT, CITED contradiction of the frozen choice, on the very term the frozen module placed outside the tolerance budget because it is worth ~4.0% at a 0.10 m skirting on a 2.50 m height. The frozen value is NOT revised; the divergence is recorded.

rules.formula: F2 wall paintable area — the opening deduction
rules.our_frozen_choice: WALL_PAINT_DEDUCTS_EVERY_STATED_OPENING = True, at the stated area
rules.fletcher_rule: In the case of deductions for doors and windows, take the full dimensions for length and height to the outside of the grounds, and not the net dimensions. In the case of doors, the height, where there is a skirting, must be taken from the top of skirting grounds, and not from the floor.
rules.note: Agrees that every opening is deducted, and specifies WHICH dimensions: the structural opening including grounds, not the clear opening. Our schema's P9 'opening area stated by the source' does not say which of the two it is, and this is the gap step 3 must close per project.

rules.our_frozen_choice: BASEBOARD_BREAKS_AT_DOOR_OPENINGS = True, full stated opening width deducted
rules.fletcher_rule_joiner: Skirtings. — Collect on 'Waste' the lengths of the several walls, making the deductions for doors, chimney-pieces, &c., and bring the total length of skirting to each room, forward in one dimension only.
rules.fletcher_rule_plasterer: Cement Skirtings. — Take the lengths and collect the same on 'Waste.' State the height, and bill and value at per foot run.
rules.agrees: THE TWO TRADES IN THE SAME BOOK DISAGREE
rules.observed_in_the_takeoff: On p.325 the cement skirting of ROOM_324B is booked at 35'6", which is the room's FULL collected girth, with the breaks numbered separately as 8 stopped ends, 2 mitres and 4 irregular. The joiner's prose rule would have deducted the three 2'10" door openings. OBSERVATION, not a settled claim: the trades differ and step 3 must match the trade before it matches the number.
rules.note: This is the contested convention the directive asks to be named as a choice. It is now contested on the page, not in the abstract.

rules.formula: F1 flooring purchase quantity — the wastage allowance
rules.our_frozen_choice: the wastage allowance is an INPUT with provenance, never a guess
rules.fletcher_rule: Where the room is irregular, it will be necessary to ascertain the average size of the flooring, so as to arrive at the net area, and make an allowance for all irregular cuttings, taking the length by a width of 3 in. for the cutting and waste.
rules.note: A cited professional precedent that a cutting-and-waste allowance is STATED as a rule with a dimension, not assumed as a percentage.

conventions: FLOORING_DEDUCTS_FIXTURE_FOOTPRINT=False (CHOICE: SMM7/NRM2 make no deduction for a void <= 0.50 m2 and no schema field states a fixture footprint; the alternative deducts them. Bound: a shower tray or chimney breast is 0.6-1.0 m2)
FLOORING_INCLUDES_DOOR_REVEAL=False (CHOICE: measured to the room face of the wall, not carried under the leaf. Bound: ~0.09 m2 per doorway)
assumptions: the floor is a single horizontal plane coincident with the room's plan outline; a split level or a stepped floor is not detectable from any schema field

the measurement convention is whatever P11 states; a comparison across two conventions measures the convention, not the engine, which is why an UNSTATED P11 is refused the accuracy claim rather than compared loosely

quantities.reason_detail: P10 does not state this room's floor finish, so there is no product and therefore no pack size; a purchase quantity without a product is a guess
P8 wall height is not stated by the source. ROOT #262 AC-4 forbids inferring it and #263 measured why a volume cannot supply it: Volume/GrossArea spans 2.045-4.225 m on one storey

conventions: CEILING_DEDUCTS_EVERY_STATED_OPENING=True (same reasoning as F2: a stated measurement is not discarded to follow a rounding rule)
assumptions: CEILING_IS_FLAT_AND_COINCIDENT_WITH_FLOOR=True. THE ASSUMPTION THAT MATTERS, AND IT IS NOT CHECKABLE: no plan-view field detects a slope, a vault or a dropped bulkhead, and #263's contract has no field for a ceiling form, so this cannot be made an input without inventing a field the contract never required. Bound: a 30 degree monopitch understates the developed area by 15.5%; a 0.4 m bulkhead around a 14 m perimeter adds 5.6 m2 of vertical face this formula does not count. Both exceed F3's 2.0% tolerance by an order of magnitude
ceiling paint covers the whole soffit: no deduction for a light fitting or a grille
